page: Microsoft Azure FX36mds is an x86_64 instance built on an Intel processor platform under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 36 dedicated vCPUs alongside 756 GB of system memory, delivering 21 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It also includes 1623 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, operating without integrated GPU hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The hardware configuration features an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 21:1, distinguishing it within memory-intensive and compute-focused infrastructure tiers. Dedicated CPU allocation provides sustained compute access across all 36 physical or virtual threads without core contention, while the 1623 GB local solid-state drive delivers rapid scratch space for disk-intensive execution pipelines.

Qualitatively, the server prioritizes resource density by pairing significant memory capacity with substantial dedicated core counts and bundled local storage. This profile eliminates the need to overprovision raw compute cores solely to acquire large memory footprints. It is structured for workloads such as large in-memory databases, memory-constrained electronic design automation (EDA), complex financial modeling, batch data analytics, and intermediate ETL operations requiring high RAM and fast temporary drive caching.
